_meta.indication: NETSPOT, after radiolabeling with Ga 68, is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult and pediatric patients.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study A (VUMC single-center expanded access study)
pivotal_trials.phase: Open-label, single-center study (originally designed as an expanded access protocol, not a formal drug-development trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Open label single center study; Ga 68 dotatate PET images read by two independent readers blinded to clinical information, compared to CT and/or MR and to indium In 111 pentetreotide SPECT images.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with known or suspected neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), predominantly gastro-entero-pancreatic
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sensitivity and specificity vs OctreoScan (In 111 pentetreotide) with a non-inferiority endpoint (primary); change in patient management (secondary).
pivotal_trials.result: Among 78 patients with available CT/MR and In 111 pentetreotide images, Ga 68 dotatate PET agreed with CT/MR in 74 patients. Of 50 patients with NETs localized by CT/MR, Ga 68 dotatate was positive in 48 (including 13 in whom In 111 pentetreotide was negative) and was negative in 26 of 28 patients in whom CT/MR was negative.

pivotal_trials.design: Diagnostic performance of Ga 68 dotatate PET in localizing tumor sites was retrospectively assessed using a reference standard (histopathology n=49 or clinical follow up up to 5 months n=55); images interpreted by consensus between two on-site readers who were not blinded to clinical information.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with suspected NETs due to clinical symptoms, elevated levels of tumor markers, or indeterminate tumors suggestive of NET
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Diagnostic performance (localization of tumor sites) of Ga 68 dotatate PET assessed against a reference standard
pivotal_trials.result: NET sites were localized by reference standard in 36 patients (all by histopathology); Ga 68 dotatate was positive, correctly identifying an NET site, in 29 and falsely negative in seven. In 68 patients with no NET identified by a reference standard, images were negative in 61 and falsely positive in seven.

pivotal_trials.design: Patients evaluated for NET recurrence using a reference standard as described for Study B; Ga 68 dotatate images interpreted independently by two central readers blinded to clinical information.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Correct localization of NETs by Ga 68 dotatate PET against a reference standard
pivotal_trials.result: Reader 1 correctly localized NETs in 23 of 29 reference standard-positive patients and reader 2 in 22. In 34 patients with no NET identified by a reference standard, reader 1 was correct in 29 and reader 2 in 32.

key_safety: The safety of Ga 68 dotatate was evaluated in three single center studies and in a survey of the scientific literature; no serious adverse reactions were identified.
target_moa: Ga 68 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors, with highest affinity for subtype 2 receptors (sstr2), which are overexpressed by many neuroendocrine tumor cells; PET images reflect the presence and density of somatostatin receptors, and Gallium 68 is a positron-emitting radionuclide enabling PET imaging.
modality: Radiopharmaceutical (kit for preparation of gallium Ga 68 dotatate injection)

rems.type: Given the favorable safety profile of the drug, no additional risk management strategies are required beyond the recommended labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; the application did not raise significant public health questions or precedent-setting regulatory/scientific issues.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan designation for the proposed use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs.

citations.quote: The product also received Orphan designation for the proposed use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs.

basis.text: Priority review granted because Netspot was judged to have the potential to improve diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management.

citations.quote: The application was granted a priority review status because Netspot was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome. The product also received Orphan designation for the proposed use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs.

summary.text: NETSPOT was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA supported by published literature and the retrospective adaptation of the Vanderbilt (VUMC) expanded access clinical experience. The application received priority review and orphan drug designation for use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs; because of the orphan designation the pediatric assessment requirement was exempt. It was approved first cycle effective June 1, 2016.

citations.quote: Advanced Accelerator Applications USA, Inc. submitted this NDA 208547 for NETSPOT as a 505(b)(2) application supported by the literature and by the retrospective adaptation of clinical experience developed at Vanderbilt University Medical Center (VUMC), from an expanded access protocol aiming to assess the clinical utility of the investigational agent for use in the management of patients with NET

The application was granted a priority review status because Netspot was judged to have the potential to improve the diagnostic accuracy for a serious condition for which an accurate diagnosis is critical for patient management and improved outcome. The product also received Orphan designation for the proposed use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs.
